raw_text:
Here’s a focused 12-week strength program tailored to a 27-year-old beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar. The plan builds foundational strength, improves pull-up capacity, and progressively overloads using tempo, leverage, unilateral work, and volume. It’s split into three 4-week phases, training 4 days/week, with optional short “grease-the-groove” pull-up practice on non-lifting days.

Overview
- Frequency: 4 days/week (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat). Optional short skill work on Wed/Sun.
- Sessions: ~45–60 minutes.
- Focus each day:
  - Day A: Upper push + pull (horizontal/vertical)
  - Day B: Lower body + core
  - Day C: Upper emphasis 2 (different angles/tempos)
  - Day D: Lower body 2 + posterior chain + core
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes. Cooldown: 5 minutes.
- Progression levers: reps, sets, tempo, ROM, leverage (incline/decline/assistance), rest times.
- Target RPE for work sets: 7–9 (2–3 reps in reserve early, 1–2 RIR later).
- Pull-up strategy: Start with eccentrics, flexed-arm hangs, scap pull-ups, assisted reps; build to full reps.

Equipment notes
- Use a sturdy chair/bench/door frame edge for incline/assisted movements.
- Use a towel for added grip variations on the bar.
- Use backpacks with books/water jugs to add load in later weeks if needed.
- For leg elevation, use a sofa or bed.

Warm-up (every session, 5–8 min)
- 1–2 minutes light cardio (march/jog in place, jumping jacks if space allows)
- Dynamic mobility: arm circles, shoulder CARs, hip circles, leg swings (front/side), thoracic rotations
- Activation: 1 set each of 8–10 reps: scapular pull-ups, glute bridges, tempo squats to bodyweight depth
- Specific warm-up: 1 easier set of first exercise

Cooldown (every session, 5 min)
- Easy breathing, slow nasal breathing 2 min
- Stretch tight areas: hip flexors, glutes, hamstrings, pecs, lats 20–30s each

PHASE 1: Foundation and Skill (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: Learn technique, build joint tolerance, establish pull-up base, introduce unilateral work and tempos.

Weekly structure (4x/week)
- Day A: Push-Pull 1
- Day B: Lower-Core 1
- Day C: Push-Pull 2
- Day D: Lower-Core 2

Week 1
Day A (Upper)
- Incline push-ups (hands on chair/sofa): 3x8–12, 3010 tempo, 90s rest
- Doorway/bar inverted rows (knees bent, feet on floor): 4x6–10, 3011, 90s
- Pike shoulder taps (hips high, partial pike): 3x6–10/side, controlled
- Assisted chin-ups (feet on chair for light support): 5x3–5, 3010, 90s
- Dead hang from bar: 3x20–30s

Day B (Lower + Core)
- Bodyweight squats: 4x10–15, 3010
- Reverse lunges: 3x8–10/leg
- Glute bridges: 4x12–15, 3011
- Calf raises (single-leg, holding doorway): 3x10–12/leg, 2s pause top
- Side plank: 3x20–30s/side
- Hollow body hold (tucked): 3x15–25s

Day C (Upper)
- Push-ups (elevated as needed to keep form): 4x6–10, 3010
- Scapular pull-ups: 3x8–12
- Eccentric chin-ups (jump to top, 4–5s down): 5x2–3, 120s rest
- Bar hangs (mixed/towel grip): 3x20–30s
- Pike push-ups (hands on floor, hips high): 3x6–8
- Band/doorway external rotations alt: If no band, do prone Y/T/W on floor 3x8 each

Day D (Lower + Posterior + Core)
- Split squats (rear foot on floor): 3x8–10/leg, 3010
- Hip hinge pattern: Good-morning bow (hands on hips, long spine) 3x10–12, 3121
- Single-leg RDL (bodyweight, balance support): 3x8–10/leg
- Step-ups onto sturdy chair/sofa edge: 3x8/leg (ensure stability)
- Plank: 3x25–35s
- Dead bug: 3x8–10/side, 3s exhale

Week 2
- Add 1–2 reps per set where possible or 1 extra set on first two movements each day.
- Keep tempos strict. Aim for total weekly pull-up practice: 30–40 quality reps (assisted/eccentric/scap).

Week 3
- Progress leverage slightly:
  - Lower incline for push-ups, elevate feet for rows (if safe), deeper split squat ROM.
  - Assisted chin-ups: reduce leg assistance; add 1–2s hold at top.
  - Eccentric chins: 3–5 total sets of 3 with 5s negatives.
- Add isometric pauses:
  - Squats and lunges: 2s pause at bottom on first 2 sets.

Week 4 (Overload then deload at week’s end)
- Early week push volume: +1 set on main push/pull and squat/lunge.
- Late week: reduce volume by 30–40% to recover (keep intensity/tempo).

PHASE 2: Strength Emphasis and Unilateral Progression (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Increase intensity via harder leverage, more single-leg patterns, introduce clusters for pulling, and tempo manipulation.

Weekly structure unchanged.

Week 5
Day A (Upper)
- Push-ups (standard, elevate hands only if needed): 5x6–10, 3010
- Inverted rows (hips higher, feet further): 5x6–8, 3111
- Chin-up clusters: 6x(1–2 reps assisted or partials) every 45–60s; aim 8–12 total reps
- Pike push-ups (harder angle or feet elevated on sofa): 4x5–8
- Hollow rocks: 3x10–15

Day B (Lower)
- Bulgarian split squats (rear foot on sofa): 4x8/leg, 3110
- Single-leg hip thrusts (shoulders on sofa): 4x8–10/leg, 2111
- Tempo squats (3s down, 1s pause): 3x12
- Nordic curl regressions on mat (kneel, hinge back with hip extension, use hands to assist): 3x6–8 slow
- Side plank with hip abduction (top leg raises): 3x8–10/side

Day C (Upper)
- Diamond or close-grip push-ups: 4x6–10
- Wide-grip inverted rows (hands wider on bar/door frame safely): 4x6–8
- Eccentric pull-ups (overhand): 5x2–3 with 5–6s down
- Flexed-arm hang (chin over bar): 3x15–25s
- Prone Y/T/W: 3x10 each

Day D (Lower + Posterior + Core)
- Cossack squat regressions (shorter range side-to-side): 3x6–8/side
- Step-downs from chair (eccentric control): 3x8/leg, 3s down
- Single-leg RDL: 4x8/leg, 3111
- Glute bridge march: 3x20 alternating
- Anti-rotation press (pallof substitute): Half-kneeling press-out with isometric hold using towel anchored in door handle (gentle), or suitcase carry hold with backpack 3x20–30s/side

Week 6
- Increase difficulty:
  - Push-ups: feet elevated for 2–3 sets if strong.
  - Rows: feet elevated on sofa for 2–3 sets.
  - Chin-up clusters: add 1 total rep; reduce assistance.
  - Split squats: increase ROM, slow 4s eccentrics on last set.
- Core: progress holds by 5–10s.

Week 7
- Intensity focus, slightly lower volume:
  - Push-ups: 4x6–8 at harder leverage, add 1–2s pause at bottom.
  - Rows: 4x6–8 with 2s squeeze at top.
  - Pull-up work: 4–5 singles or doubles at highest quality (assisted or partials from top range), then 2 sets of 5s negatives.
  - Bulgarian split squats: 4x6–8 with 2s pause bottom.
  - Single-leg RDL: 3x6–8 with slow tempo.

Week 8 (Overreach early, deload late)
- Early week: add 1 set to main compound each day and an extra chin-up cluster.
- Late week (last 2 sessions): cut volume by 40–50%, keep form crisp to set up Phase 3.

PHASE 3: Peak Relative Strength and Pull-Up Achievement (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Maximize strength with harder leverage, lower reps, more isometrics, aim for first strict bodyweight chin-up or add reps if already achieved.

Week 9
Day A (Upper)
- Push-ups (feet elevated 20–40 cm): 5x4–6, 3110
- Inverted rows (feet elevated): 5x4–6, 2112
- Chin-up strength sets: 6x1–2 reps (assisted as lightly as possible or full if capable), 90s
- Pike push-ups to target shoulders (hips high): 4x5–7
- Hollow body hold (full or one-leg extended): 3x25–35s

Day B (Lower)
- Bulgarian split squats: 5x6/leg, 3111
- Single-leg hip thrusts: 4x6–8/leg with 2s top squeeze
- Tempo squats (4s down, 1s pause): 3x10
- Nordic regressions: 4x5 slow
- Side plank reach-throughs: 3x10/side

Day C (Upper)
- Close-grip push-ups with 2s pause at bottom: 4x5–7
- Row isometric top holds: 4x5 reps with 3s hold each rep
- Pull-up negatives with mid-range isometric: 4x2 reps, 5–6s down + 3s hold at 90°
- Flexed-arm hang (overhand): 3x20–30s
- Prone Y/T/W: 3x12 each

Day D (Lower + Posterior + Core)
- Step-downs (higher chair if safe): 4x6–8/leg, 3–4s eccentric
- Skater squats to mat (assisted balance): 3x5–6/leg
- Single-leg RDL: 4x6/leg, 3112
- Hip hinge good-mornings: 3x12
- Dead bug with band alternative: slow 3x10/side
- Farmer hold with backpack (heavy): 3x30–45s

Week 10
- Aim to hit first full chin-up if close: test after warm-up on Day A; then complete plan.
- Chin-ups: move to 5–6 sets of 2 reps if you can do singles; otherwise stay at 1–2 assisted reps, slightly less assistance than Week 9.
- Push-ups/rows: Slightly increase leverage or add backpack load if reps exceed top ranges.
- Lower: Add 1–2 reps per set or a pause at bottom.

Week 11
- Intensify, slightly lower volume:
  - Push-ups (hard leverage): 4x4–6
  - Rows (hard leverage): 4x4–6
  - Chin-ups: 6–8 singles at highest quality; rest 90–120s
  - Bulgarian split squats: 4x5–6 slow, deep
  - Single-leg RDL: 3x5–6
  - Core holds +10–15s vs Week 9

Week 12 (Taper and Test)
- Early week: Maintain intensity, cut volume ~30%.
- Testing day (end of week):
  - Max strict push-ups (good form)
  - Max inverted rows (controlled)
  - Max full chin-ups or best negative (10s) if not yet there
  - Split squat 1-set AMRAP/leg at good form
  - Hollow hold max time
- Non-testing sessions: Technique work, mobility, and light sets (2–3 sets, RPE 6–7).

Pull-up progression details (add-on)
- Grease-the-groove (optional, 3–5 days/week on non-sessions): 2–3 mini-sets throughout the day:
  - Week 1–2: Scap pull-ups 5–6 reps + 10–20s dead hang
  - Week 3–4: 1–2 eccentric reps (5s) + 10–20s hang
  - Week 5–6: 1–2 assisted chin-ups (easy) + 10–20s hang
  - Week 7–8: Singles with minimal assist or partials from top
  - Week 9–12: 1–2 clean singles if possible; never to failure

Progression rules
- When you hit top of rep range with clean form on all sets, progress:
  - Make leverage harder (lower hand elevation or elevate feet)
  - Add time-under-tension (slower eccentrics, pauses)
  - Add a 5–10 kg backpack for push-ups, rows, split squats, hip thrusts (Weeks 8–12 if safe)
- Rest times:
  - Compounds: 90–120s
  - Assistance/core: 45–75s
- RPE: Start at 7–8; peak weeks allow 8–9; deload at 6–7.

Technique cues (key moves)
- Push-ups: Straight line head–heels, elbows ~30–45°, full chest-to-hand depth.
- Rows: Pull chest to bar/edge, squeeze shoulder blades, avoid shrugging.
- Chin/pull-ups: Start from dead hang, depress scapula, pull elbows down, no kipping.
- Squats/split squats: Tripod foot, knee tracks toes, tall torso.
- Hip hinges/RDL: Hips back, neutral spine, feel hamstrings.
- Core: Ribcage down, breathe behind brace.

Recovery
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night.
- Walking: 20–30 minutes on non-lifting days for recovery.
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes daily focused on hips, T-spine, lats/pecs.
- Deloads built into Weeks 4, 8, 12.

Basic nutrition guidance (if client requests more, expand)
- Protein: ~1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day.
- Calories: Slight surplus if muscle gain is priority (+200–300 kcal/day), or maintenance for body recomposition.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day, add more if sweating.
- Pre-session: Light meal 1–2 hours before (protein + carbs).
- Post-session: Protein serving (20–40 g) within a few hours; whole-food carbs.
- Creatine monohydrate optional: 3–5 g/day, consistent timing.

Safety and environment
- Ensure the pull-up bar and chair/sofa are stable and rated for weight.
- Use controlled tempos to minimize injury risk in a small space.
- Stop sets 1–2 reps before form breaks; no failure on eccentrics more than once per week.

Deliverables for the client
- Provide a simple weekly checklist with exercises and boxes for sets/reps completed.
- Track pull-up total weekly volume and best single rep quality.
- Reassess form via short videos Weeks 2, 6, 10 for push-up, row, split squat, chin-up mechanics.

This plan builds serious relative strength with only a mat and pull-up bar, giving your client clear weekly structure, measurable progression, and safe overload paths.
